report:
The manuscript's principal finite-contact results, coupled examples, and sequence-independent completion construction check out in their stated coefficient and approximation domains. However, Theorem 11 additionally calls the literal operator a “uniform-continuous extension,” and native note n4 repeats an unqualified uniform-continuity guarantee. Global uniform continuity for the stated bounded-continuous-test weak uniformity is false. The proof establishes continuity under uniform convergence and quantitative continuity on families with a common bound relative to γ. Those statements do not establish the additional global guarantee. Because this review requires every assertion of the unchanged paper and notes to hold, the verdict is FAIL as written.

A counterexample already lies in the literal category. Take the balanced unit-weight line X=R and γ(x)=|x|. Put A_n(x)=|x−2n| and B_n(x)=|x−2n−1/(8n)|. Both are relative literal PA PC functions on finite rational structures, and both belong to the declared regularizable domain. Their uniform distance is 1/(8n), tending to zero. Primitive recursion gives MA(A_n)=2δ_(2n) and MA(B_n)=2δ_(2n+1/(8n)). For the single bounded continuous test ψ(x)=sin(πx²), its value at 2n is zero, while its value at 2n+1/(8n) is cos(π/(64n²)), tending to one. The difference of the measure integrals therefore tends in absolute value to two. Thus this fixed C_b evaluation of the operator is not globally uniformly continuous.

The real category also fails a global uniform-continuity assertion even for a fixed bounded Lipschitz test. For even n, set a_j=4j for even j and a_j=4j+1 for odd j; set b_j=4j+1 for even j and b_j=4j for odd j, with 0≤j<n. Define A_n=n^−1 Σ_j|x−a_j| and B_n=n^−1 Σ_j|x−b_j|. These are rational-affine relative PA PC functions. Consecutive opposite displacements cancel, giving 0≤A_n−B_n≤2/n and uniform distance 2/n. Their raw measures are (2/n)Σ_jδ_(a_j) and (2/n)Σ_jδ_(b_j). Let η be the continuous eight-periodic function obtained by linear interpolation through (0,1/4), (1,−1/4), (4,−1/4), (5,1/4), (8,1/4). It is bounded and Lipschitz, equals 1/4 at every a_j and −1/4 at every b_j, and the difference of its measure integrals is exactly one. This also excludes a global modulus in the usual bounded-Lipschitz weak metric.

These examples do not contradict the manuscript's convergence theorem for uniformly convergent approximating families: their relative bounds grow with n. They identify exactly why its proof cannot yield the extra global conclusion. The moment constant K depends on a common C bounding |a_i−γ|. Such a C exists for a uniformly convergent family, but there is no fixed C over the entire relative domain. Replacing “uniform-continuous” by “continuous under uniform convergence,” restricting the guarantee to fixed relative sup-bounds, or explicitly specifying compact-test/vague uniform continuity would change the scope of the asserted guarantee. I have not silently adopted such a replacement.

I independently checked the complete supplied TeX, its mathematical argument, material-change record, ledger applications, and all seven native-final notes. The prior196 discussion was not used as a mathematical grant. Only the complete A224/B225/R230 grants and their unchanged clarifications were accepted without reproof. A224 supplies context rather than a theorem on the present two-plane space. B225 applies to inherited finite positive balanced stars, including common lineality, and to noncompactness only in its finite globally embedded pure positive-dimensional category. R230 applies to finite-valued printed-PC competitors, continuous references and bounded continuous obstacles here. Its unrestricted-envelope identification preserves the actual upper growth bound. Its rational cone arguments also have the requisite hypotheses in the nonbalanced polyhedral applications of Theorem 13. The unindexed task passage records this grant authorization and is not external-source coverage.

I opened the original [BBGS publisher PDF](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf) and checked the requested definitions and complete 3.12/3.15/3.18/3.19 chain, including all subdivision cases and both double-sum interchanges. Its hypotheses match this finite application. I also checked the literal definitions and pertinent elementary units in [BMPS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). Neither its broad extension theorem nor its density/regularity equivalences were imported. BBGS's real-endpoint convention was not transferred to the printed rational-endpoint class.

The primitive-to-unit conversion is correct at every recursive dimension. Saturation makes a basis of N_τ followed by a primitive quotient lift a basis of N_σ. Thus the projected lift has inward height a_σ/a_τ. Multiplying lattice weights by a_σ gives Euclidean-balanced weights. After subtracting an ambient extension of the face derivative, continuity cancels tangent contributions and balancing cancels the extension's contribution. Consequently B_(−f)(ac)(τ)=a_τ D_f c(τ). Applying this identity successively, including signed or zero intermediate weights, ends with a_v=1 and the exact primitive raw atom. No extra factorial appears. Tangential changes of lifts cancel directly. The codimension-two quotient has two boundary rays even for nonsimplicial cells; common lineality is removed in that quotient. Local supports give positivity at each intermediate balanced cycle.

Lemmas 1–3 are sound. The segment maximum argument correctly proves ordinary segment convexity from continuous local supports, and propagation of the center support proves every real-endpoint PCC inequality. Divisor applications use PA functions and a common carrying structure; the support agrees with the derivative along the center face. In Lemma 2, dependent-column elimination reduces nonnegative representations to finitely many independent subsets with bounded inverse maps, proving cone closedness. Nearest-point separation has the correct sign and gives λ≥0, Uλ=0 and λ·s<0 when a support is infeasible. Tests at rational representatives extend over every real point of each face because the germ's cones and linear parts are fixed there. Extreme positive kernel rays have one-dimensional kernels on their supports, hence support size at most rank(U)+1, and rational circuit generators suffice. Lineality and nonsimplicial stars are retained.

The corrected strict-floor lemma explicitly assumes PC/nonnegative relation costs. B225 supplies positive spanning, not positivity of those costs. With PC established, the normalized relation section is nonempty compact, and absence of zero cost gives a positive minimum θ. Separating s−δ1 for 0<δ<θ produces strictly positive generator residuals. A quantitative bound is δ|x|/max_i|d_i|. Opposite lineality generators give a flat relation. The retained negative-slope line example correctly disproves the old unconditional lemma.

Theorems 4–5 and Corollary 6 are sound in the finite-PA sector. The envelope is PC by supremum Jensen inequalities, so Theorem 4 establishes PC before applying the repaired floor lemma. Its raised affine floor preserves the obstacle inequality and growth, agrees on a strict collar, and has supports at active and tie points. It is an unrestricted competitor; rational PA membership is unnecessary. In Theorem 5, scaling the flat relation to rational norm-boundary endpoints preserves the barycenter and zero average slope cost. Rational radial chords give the upper bound inside the roof, the obstacle gives it outside, and shrinking rational simplices extend it to all real centers without continuity of competitors. The endpoint is actual relative PA PC and therefore regularizable. Refinement independence eliminates all artificial atoms. The exact integral is −Rm_v. Both directions of Corollary 6 retain the actual-reference and coefficient-category hypotheses.

The fixed-structure certificate is exact. It includes continuity on shared faces, PC circuit inequalities at every face, equality of all recession slopes, zero extreme-relation cost, and strict positivity of the actual degree-d raw mass polynomial. Vertex-plus-recession decomposition proves that the recession equations are precisely bounded difference. Saturated normals and actual top weights enter every recursive coefficient. Real feasibility does not establish literal feasibility. Genuine common lineality with affine invariance forces zero top atom on a carrying generalized fan; mere flatness along an isolated line does not. No refinement bound or all-envelope conclusion follows from the fixed system.

The coupled PA example is correct. Each coordinate plane is saturated and unit-balanced, including the four transverse classes on their shared axis. On the xz plane, h=max(|x|,|z|)+|z| has axis weights two and diagonal weights one; outgoing slopes one and two give raw origin mass twelve. On the yz plane, g=max(|y|−1,|z|)+|z| has central-axis weight four, outer-axis weights two, and graph-ray weights one. At each p_±, primitive directions have weights 4,2,1,1 and slopes 0,1,2,2, giving mass six and the displayed balance. The central-origin yz contribution is zero. All zero walls and subdivision cancellations are accounted for. Hence MA(γ)=24δ_0 and MA(f)=12δ_0+6δ_(p_+)+6δ_(p_−). Positive growth and −1≤f−γ≤0 hold. The radius-1/4 roof has unrestricted envelope f and integral −3. The corner differences −1/4 for γ and f and +1/4 for u exclude precisely the specified cross-times-z additive decomposition. Total mass and polygon area are checks, not operator substitutes.

The irrational-kink example is also correct. Its maximum is |x−t|+t with irrational t=√2/2, so it has no finite rational carrying structure. Rational t_n decreasing to t give literal convex approximants with exact uniform error 2(t_n−t). The example establishes failure of finite real-PA maximum closure, not failure of regularization.

Theorem 7 and Corollary 8 are sound for rational-affine positive-growth references in the real category. Finite vertex/recession decomposition gives γ≥aρ−b with a>0. A slower rational ambient norm therefore lies below γ outside a compact set. Raising it above γ near v and inserting a sufficiently small scaled jet yields the stated strict collar, supports at ties, exact germ C+t+δh, bounded actual-reference difference, and atom δ^d m_0(h). All new walls are rational. The rational approximation argument includes shared-face and every PC constraint, a rational extreme zero-cost equation, and active constraints at cone-boundary points. Strict positivity of the mass polynomial persists even with specified positive real top weights. The corollary then follows from the finite contact and roof results, with its universal refinement quantifier intact. There is no literal gluing or irrational-reference maximum closure claim.

Lemma 9 has the correct signs. A bounded affine function has zero slope on every unbounded edge of the common finite one-cycle. A bounded edge contributes −Z(e)ΔbΔc/L_e, which is symmetric. Its outgoing degree contributions cancel. Replacing mixed factors by γ one at a time therefore preserves total raw mass M. Applying bounded integration by parts to γ−q and a_1−γ yields exactly the printed relative identity. Positivity and balanced preservation apply to the intermediate cycles, including zero weights.

Lemma 10 and its density argument are sound. A finite rational wall arrangement permits H=KΣ|L_j| with both H and H+ψ ambient convex. Scaling H below the reference recession growth and making it strictly dominate γ on a neighborhood of the test support gives actual rational-affine relative PC functions θ_0,θ_1 with θ_1−θ_0=εψ. Their open local descriptions cover support boundaries and ties. Rational bump nets approximate C_c(X) uniformly with supports in a fixed larger compact set. For tests inside an open equality set, the scale can be chosen below the distance of the compact test support from its complement, retaining support inside that open set. No C_b density assertion is needed.

Apart from the extra uniform-continuity wording identified above, Theorem 11's completion proof is valid. Telescoping and edge integration by parts give the compact rational-test bound (2M/ε)Σ_i||a_i−b_i||_∞ for arbitrary real affine approximants. Density and the common mass bound extend Cauchy convergence to C_c. The positive functional's open-set construction gives a finite metric outer measure: compact partitions establish countable subadditivity, separated sets establish metric additivity, and compact cutoffs give regularity. Range-step approximations identify its integrals with the functional, proving the required Radon representation and uniqueness.

For tightness, after a rational constant shift makes γ nonnegative, q_j=max(γ−j,0) is an actual rational-affine relative PA PC function. Splitting a_i−q_j into a_i−γ and γ−q_j in the relative identity and iterating gives the printed bound 2dCM+∫γ MA(γ). The reference measure has finite support. Monotone truncation yields a uniform γ-moment bound for a fixed uniformly bounded relative family. Properness then gives tightness, exact limiting mass M and convergence against every C_b test. Comparing arbitrary approximants proves independence. The localized test bound proves equality on open subsets; symmetry passes from finite recursion. Extraction with error 2^−n and rational additions 4·2^−n gives genuinely decreasing approximants. No merely continuous PC function is added to the domain. Corollary 12 correctly retains domain membership and all R230 hypotheses and follows from uniform envelope convergence and bounded-test measure convergence.

The non-PA example and its explicit measure are correct. The even quadratic transition is convex and gives −3/2≤F−γ≤0. Dyadic chords have the stated slopes, initial/final half-jumps, monotonicity and exact error 1/(8N²). Their maxima are actual relative real PA PC functions on finite rational structures. Primitive graph tangents (q,p) and Bezout quotient lifts give weights 1/q. Vertical kink walls give Δ_j and axis walls give two. The initial vertex has mass 6Δ_0; subsequent axis and upper/lower graph vertices have masses 4Δ_j,Δ_j,Δ_j, with the displayed balances and slopes. Reflection supplies the negative side; the horizontal sheet contributes twelve and the central vertical contribution is zero. The jumps sum to one, giving raw total twenty-four.

The compactly supported Riemann sums converge to exactly the printed pushforward parameter measure: origin mass twelve, two segment measures of density four and four parabolic parameter measures of density one. The extra moments in n5 are indeed ∫y²=28 and ∫z²=1/5. No Euclidean arc-length density or inverse surrogate is used. The shared PA germ inside the roof gives the unrestricted envelopes F_N and F; the extended-domain antecedent is supplied by the decreasing approximation. The contact integral is −3, and the mixed differences persist. The quadratic restriction proves non-PA status of F and U. The midpoint integral-slope argument gives the literal approximation gap 3/64. No literal measure is assigned to F.

Theorem 13 is sound without balancing. A finite polyhedral space has finitely many components, so noncompactness supplies a noncompact connected component. The compactly supported gap D=max(γ,C)−γ vanishes on every unbounded affine carrying cell. A cell path from a positive gap to the unbounded region forces a bounded positive-dimensional cell with nonzero gap slope. Integral norm cones globally majorize D/N and match every fractional vertex value; their finite minimum with D gives a bounded literal obstacle. Pointed vertex/recession representations, rational far endpoints and shrinking simplices prove the exact unrestricted envelope γ+D/N. On the chosen primitive segment its noninteger slope yields the stated positive quantization gap for every literal PC approximant. B225 is applied afterward only in its finite globally embedded pure positive-balanced scope. Dimension zero and abstract compact chart spaces retain their separate scopes.

Harmless clarifications are limited to notation and already determined proof references: BBGS Proposition 3.19's commutation step cites 3.12 but uses 3.15; decreasing may mean nonincreasing, although the new extraction is strictly decreasing; and n5's counts 8,14,26 are yz-sheet positive-vertex counts, with the fixed xz origin adding one to the full-space counts. Its raw measure formula already distinguishes those contributions. The global uniform-continuity issue is not included in these harmless corrections.

The old whole247/196 FAIL remains intact: its unconditional floor lemma was false and its old endpoint was separable. The present PC hypothesis repair and replacement coupled functions are explicit material changes, independently checked here. Historical hashes, registration records, builds, finite grids and requested model routing were treated as provenance data, not mathematical premises. No saved source was edited. Original P05.2 remains open and candidate=false; this review does not close its full real-reference classification or grant all-obstacle regularization.

premises: For a Euclidean quasi-embedded space X, open U, common complex Π, real PA functions f,g carried by Π and real k-weight c on Π|U, BBGS2022's negative inward-unit-conormal product commutes with restriction and subdivision; when k≥2, f·(g·c)=g·(f·c). A weight is Minkowski iff (ℓ∘ι)·c=0 for every ambient linear ℓ. Restriction, subdivision and PA products preserve Minkowski weights, including signed and zero weights; no strict positivity is required (Definitions 3.1–3.9, Propositions 3.12, 3.15, 3.19, Lemma 3.18).

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 uses finite globally embedded rational complexes, saturated tangent lattices Nσ=N∩span_R(σ−σ), rational cycle weights, primitive inward quotient normals, and continuous PA functions with integral tangent linear parts and rational constants. Definitions 3.2–3.3 restrict PCC endpoints to rational points while allowing real centers and coefficients. Definitions 2.31 and 4.4–4.7 define the raw measure by d primitive-divisor intersections with the tangent correction and no additional factorial. Definition 3.23 specifies uniform relative PA completion; Definition 4.15 requires strictly positive nonzero recession slopes. For its PA PC reference γ positive at infinity and continuous u, Definition 6.2 defines the envelope as sup{q∈PC:q≤γ+u, q≤γ+O(1)}, with −∞ for an empty competitor set. Definition 6.9 presupposes pair-level regularity before orthogonality.

BBGS2022 Definition 5.1 permits arbitrary endpoints xi∈U, nonnegative real coefficients summing to one, and barycenter ι(x)=Σν_iι(x_i). PCCs require a center face τ containing x and endpoint faces σ_i containing τ and contained in U. No rational-point restriction is imposed.
